teaser.text: Severn Trent supplies water, removes wastewater and maintains the infrastructure that makes both services possible. Its money comes mainly from regulated bills, then flows into operating costs, construction and the long-term renewal of a system that customers depend on.

stock.title: Severn Trent stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Severn Trent's stock forecast weighs bear, base and bull scenarios against cash flow, debt, regulated returns and today's valuation.
stock.opening: The weighted forecast for Severn Trent is 2475.95p in October 2027 and reaches 3598.04p by October 2029. Severn Trent's outcome hinges on funding AMP8 and earning regulated returns from its investment.
stock.closing: The full memo also answers how Severn Trent's business works, who its rivals are, how management is performing and what risks could change the outlook.

blocks.heading: Where could Severn Trent's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted price is 2475.95p in October 2027, implying a loss of 18% including dividends. By October 2029, it reaches 3598.04p, implying a gain of 25%. The forecast assigns 25% to the bear case, 55% to the base case and 20% to the bull case.

The weighted forecast points to a difficult first year, followed by recovery. The weighted price is 2475.95 in October 2027, an 18% loss with dividends. It reaches 3026.19 in October 2028, a 3% gain. By October 2029 it reaches 3598.04, a 25% gain.

blocks.heading: What has to go right, and what could go wrong for Severn Trent?

paragraphs.text: The bear case gives earnings of £390m initially and £420m thereafter. It reaches only £450m because higher interest, operating costs, delays and environmental charges absorb much of the regulated growth. The bull case starts at £550m and reaches £720m. It ends at £900m if efficiency savings, timely investment and service incentives offset financing costs. FY26 already delivered £36m of efficiencies and £18m of energy savings, but free cash flow was negative £1,045m and debt reached £10,880m.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Severn Trent really make?

paragraphs.text: The dividend is not being paid from surplus cash after all investment. In FY26, operational cash was £1.212bn. Cash capital expenditure was £1.884bn, and net interest paid was £341m. Free cash flow was therefore negative £1.046bn, while dividends were £371m; adjusted net debt rose by £1.509bn. That may be sensible if the new infrastructure later earns regulated income, but it makes financing part of the investment case.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Severn Trent today?

paragraphs.text: A trailing P/E divides today’s price by the last twelve months of earnings. A forward P/E uses an estimate for the next twelve months, so it falls when expected earnings rise. The forward valuation implies about 205p of earnings per share, but that is a forecast. Severn Trent’s adjusted FY26 EPS was 184.4p, compared with statutory EPS of 123.5p. Adjusted earnings exclude items including deferred tax and financial-instrument gains or losses, so the definitions must match before growth can be judged.

blocks.heading: How much does Severn Trent pay per share?

paragraphs.text: Dividends begin at £1.305 in every case, matching guidance. The base case rises to £1.338 and then £1.371, following 2.5% annual CPIH growth. The bear case holds at £1.305 before cutting to £1.20 as cash pressure intensifies. The bull case reaches £1.357 and then £1.411 because stronger delivery permits faster growth. The policy targets annual CPIH growth, but the negative cash flow and rising interest bill limit confidence.

blocks.heading: What could change Severn Trent's dividend?

paragraphs.text: The November 2026 interim results will test whether capital spending and interest are beginning to overwhelm operating cash. Further deterioration in free cash flow, debt headroom or funding access would move the forecast towards the bear case.

earnings.closing: The full memo also answers how Severn Trent's business works, who its rivals are, how management is paid, and what risks it faces.

blocks.heading: What has Severn Trent guided for FY27?

paragraphs.text: Management targets at least 250p of adjusted EPS in FY28. It also plans £2,200–£2,500 million of capital investment in FY27.

Management’s promise is higher underlying earnings alongside the company’s largest investment programme. Adjusted basic earnings per share, or EPS, is profit attributed to each share after specified items are removed; it is not cash available for shareholders.

blocks.heading: What do Severn Trent's last eight reported periods show?

paragraphs.text: Revenue, operating income, net income and diluted EPS all improved in the six months to March 2026. The September 2025 half also improved against its predecessor, which makes the annual recovery broader than one unusually strong closing period. Both comparisons benefited from the same new price settlement, however, so they do not establish that the growth will recur once that settlement enters the comparative year.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in Severn Trent's next results?

paragraphs.text: The 18 November 2026 interim results should show whether construction is accelerating, financing costs remain manageable and liquidity is being replenished. Progress against the FY27 performance-incentive target matters, but earned incentives and collected cash arrive at different times.
The £239 million consumer claim remains contingent, with the Supreme Court hearing listed for 8–9 February 2027. These events will test more than earnings: they will test compliance and cash.
